name: Power management and electrical SCADA
principle: A power management system supervises generation, tie-lines and major loads: it schedules and dispatches running generator sets, synchronises and parallels them, maintains frequency and voltage, arms staged load shedding for generator or tie loss, and manages islanding and re-synchronisation with the grid. PMS logic sits on electrical SCADA above the protection relays and complements them — protection clears faults in milliseconds while the PMS re-balances the network in seconds.

process_steps.name: Network measured from IEDs and meters over IEC 61850/Modbus
Generation dispatched and synchronised against demand and reserve targets
Staged load shedding armed and executed on disturbance
Islanding, closed-bus transfer and re-sync managed

limitations: PMS misbehaviour in transient studies is a classic commissioning risk; full simulation testing is required
load-shed priority lists must track the current process state to stay safe
advantages: keeps island networks stable through large motor starts and unit trips
reduces installed generation margin by managing demand actively
